item.title: King’s Lynn arts society reaches milestone with food bank donation
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn arts society reaches milestone with food bank donation
The Arts Society King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone by donating its 1,000th art and craft pack to the town’s food bank. The project, which began in 2020, provides children from families using the food bank with creative materials and a reading book for Christmas. Each gift is presented in a handmade fabric bag, created with support from Norfolk Creative Arts and the Wootton Crafters.
Funding for this year’s packs was provided by local businesses and charities, including Mars Foods and Hayes and Storr Solicitors. Distribution of the gifts is scheduled to begin at the start of December. Food bank officials have expressed their gratitude for the ongoing support, noting the positive impact these donations have on local families.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nominations closing for 2027 West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
Businesses in West Norfolk have just one week left to submit nominations for the 2027 Mayor’s Business Awards. Organisers are particularly encouraging entries for the Environmental Champion category, which recognises firms demonstrating a strong commitment to sustainability and reducing their environmental impact.
The awards, now in their 38th year, feature 11 different categories. Nominations must be submitted by 5pm on Friday, November 27. The winners will be announced at a ceremony held at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn on Friday, March 5. Last year’s Environmental Champion award was presented to British Sugar’s Wissington site for their work in reducing carbon emissions. Further details on how to enter can be found via the Lynn News.

item.title: Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
Norfolk County Council’s Health Overview Scrutiny Committee has examined a new ‘Case for Change’ report from the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group. The review outlines potential service adjustments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, citing workforce shortages and a projected £53 million deficit by 2034.
Councillors raised concerns that proposed changes could force West Norfolk residents to travel to Norwich for care. During the meeting, Councillor Alexandra Kemp warned that longer travel times on the A47 could negatively impact patient outcomes. While no final decisions have been made, the committee has called for greater transparency and clarity regarding the potential impact on local families and the wider healthcare system.

item.title: Wisbech teenager disqualified for drink-driving
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech teenager disqualified for drink-driving
A 19-year-old woman from Wisbech has been banned from the roads after being caught drink-driving in King’s Lynn. Juste Kantautaite, of Southwell Road, was stopped by police on Blackfriars Road at 4:20am on October 18. Officers conducted a breath test after finding her stationary vehicle, which revealed she had 61mcg of alcohol in 100ml of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35mcg.
At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, the court heard that Kantautaite had been persuaded to drink while celebrating a friend’s birthday. She pleaded guilty to the offence and has been disqualified from driving for 17 months. In addition to the ban, she must pay a £400 fine, a £160 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

item.title: Medical records accessed unlawfully at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Medical records accessed unlawfully at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
New figures reveal that staff at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn accessed medical records without authorisation on 107 occasions between 2021 and 2026. Hospital management stated that while most incidents involved employees viewing their own files, one case concerned a patient’s records. That specific matter was investigated and reported to the Information Commissioner’s Office.
The hospital’s director of people and culture, Zoe Baxter, emphasised that staff are regularly reminded that accessing records for personal reasons is unlawful. Across the country, over 3,000 similar incidents were recorded by NHS staff during the same five-year period. The East of England Ambulance Service Trust reported 182 cases of inappropriate access within that timeframe.
